st.text: judge-jev tests MUST run offline against recorded Jev answers.
judge-jev tests MUST NOT depend on timing.
judge-jev tests MUST NOT depend on sleeps.
judge-jev tests MUST NOT depend on ordering.
judge-jev MUST obtain records through Raptor's query interface.
judge-jev MUST NOT parse record Markdown itself.

judge-jev MUST NOT run SQL (Structured Query Language) against the record
store itself.
judge-jev MUST send every Jev request through one batch command.
The batch command MUST read request lines.
The batch command MUST write one result envelope per request.
The batch command MUST use typed error codes.
The batch command MUST apply a fixed retry policy.
The batch command MUST enforce request size limits.

The batch command MUST log every request through the sc-observability
logger (REQ-JEV-0008).

The batch command MUST log every answer through the sc-observability
logger (REQ-JEV-0008).

judge-jev MUST read the TypeSafe API key from `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` first,
then from the platform credential store, service `plan-anchor`, account
`typesafe-api-key`.

judge-jev MUST refuse every live Jev call with
`POLICY.REMOTE_JUDGE_DISABLED` unless the committed
`.sc/judge-jev/settings.yaml` sets `allow_remote_judge: true`.
judge-jev MUST NOT write that setting without the user's answer.
judge-jev MUST ship as a marketplace plugin for Claude.
judge-jev MUST ship as a marketplace plugin for Codex.
judge-jev MUST ship as a marketplace plugin for Cursor.
An upgrade MUST update every harness that is locked, installed or present.

judge-jev MUST obtain its record database by asking Raptor to build a
local SQLite database from the repository's Raptor-parseable Markdown on
each run.

When Raptor supplies a SQLite snapshot of a Dolt branch, judge-jev MUST
query it through the same Raptor interface.

judge-jev's requirements, non-functional requirements and decisions MUST
import through Raptor with no issues.

judge-jev MUST write its run logs (requests, answers, quality-tree
branches, verdicts) through the sc-observability logger, the logger
sc-agent uses.
judge-jev MUST NOT keep its own log format alongside it.

judge-jev MUST provide a mode that reports, for one requirement (REQ),
non-functional requirement (NFR) or architecture decision record (ADR),
the verdict of that record kind's quality decision tree.

The mode MUST judge only records that Raptor imported without
diagnostics.

The mode MUST run as a decision tree of prompts: each wave sends several
questions, and the answers to one wave select the next wave's questions.

Every wave MUST report, as its reason, each of its questions with the
question's id and text, Jev's choice and Jev's confidence.

A wave the tree marks per statement MUST send one request for each MUST
and MUST NOT statement of the record, carrying that statement with the
whole record as context.

A per-statement wave's reason MUST list each statement's index and text
with each question's id, choice and confidence.

A per-statement wave's verdict rule MUST be able to fire when any one
statement's answers match it.

A per-statement wave's verdict MUST name the statements whose answers
fired its rule.

A per-statement request that gets no answer MUST fail with an error that
names its statement.
A wave after the first MUST refine the answers of the wave before it.

A wave after the first MUST be designed from the observed live results
of the wave before it.

A wave with no next wave MUST end the walk, with its verdict given by a
rule in the tree file over that wave's answers.

The tree MUST ship with the tool as a data file a consumer can override
(REQ-JEV-0205); answers select the branch and the verdict, never a model
choosing the next questions.
A failing answer MUST report the decision-tree path that failed.

A live run MUST log every wave as output: its composed request, Jev's
answers, its reason and the branch or verdict they selected.
The mode MUST NOT check structure that Raptor's import checks.

`judge-jev check` MUST take one of two argument forms: a single record
with a location and a mode, or a `--profile`.

In the single-record form, `judge-jev check` MUST take one record id,
given with exactly one record-kind flag: `--req` (requirement), `--adr`
(architecture decision record) or `--nfr` (non-functional requirement).

In the single-record form, `judge-jev check` MUST take exactly one
`--location`.

In the single-record form, `judge-jev check` MUST take exactly one
`--mode`.
Each record kind MUST use its own question set.
Each Jev request MUST carry exactly one record.
Each Jev request MUST carry exactly one location.
A run over many pairs MUST send them as a stream of single requests.
judge-jev MUST support the target mode `prompt`.
judge-jev MUST support the target mode `skill`.
judge-jev MUST support the target mode `task`.
judge-jev MUST support the target mode `code`.
In `task` mode judge-jev MUST judge the raw template.

In `task` mode judge-jev MUST judge an assignment rendered by sc-compose
in strict mode from the vars file that `--vars` names, or, in a profile
run, that the profile names.

In `code` mode judge-jev MUST resolve the location with the tree-sitter
grammars sc-agent defines.
judge-jev MUST NOT define its own tree-sitter grammars.

judge-jev MUST read a TOML profile listing locations, each with its
mode, the record ids that govern it, and for `task` mode a vars file.
`judge-jev check --profile <profile>` MUST check every listed pair.
`judge-jev check --profile <profile>` MUST report each pair's verdict.

`judge-jev check --profile <profile>` MUST aggregate the verdicts per
record.

`judge-jev check --profile <profile>` MUST aggregate the verdicts per
location.
A profile run MUST NOT judge a pair the profile does not list.

judge-jev MUST ship one question set per combination of record kind and
target class (agent text or code).
judge-jev MUST ship one quality decision tree per record kind.

Every shipped question and prompt text MUST be approved by Rand before
it ships.
Question sets MUST be data files shipped with the tool.
Quality decision trees MUST be data files shipped with the tool.
The released tool MUST accept an override file for any question set.

The released tool MUST accept an override file for any quality decision
tree.
Every result MUST carry the question-set id.
Every result MUST carry the content digest of the file used.
Every log entry MUST carry the question-set id.
Every log entry MUST carry the content digest of the file used.

When a record is satisfied in more than one location (prompt, skill,
agent, template or code), judge-jev MUST judge the record separately at
each location.
judge-jev MUST report one result per (record, location) pair.
judge-jev MUST NOT combine a record's locations into one judgment.

A location MUST take one of three forms: `path`, `path#Heading` or
`path::Symbol`.
A `path` location MUST select the whole file.

A `path#Heading` location MUST select a Markdown section, from the
heading to the next heading of the same or higher level.

A `path::Symbol` location MUST select a code symbol resolved by
sc-agent's tree-sitter grammars.

Markdown sections MUST be parsed by the same rules Raptor uses for the
same file.
A location MUST NOT be a line range.
`judge-jev quality` MUST accept `--dry-run`.
`judge-jev check` MUST accept `--dry-run`.
A dry run MUST compose every request without calling Jev.
Each dry-run entry MUST report the record id.
Each dry-run entry MUST report the record's Raptor source.

Each dry-run entry MUST report the resolved location as its path, section
or symbol.

Each dry-run entry MUST report the digest of the location's selected
text.
Each dry-run entry MUST report the mode.

Each dry-run entry MUST report the question set as its shipped id or its
override path.
In `task` mode, each dry-run entry MUST report the vars file.
In `task` mode, each dry-run entry MUST report the rendered text.
Each dry-run entry MUST report the full composed request.

Each dry-run entry MUST report the composed request's size against the
request limit.
For `quality`, the dry run MUST report the decision tree.
For `quality`, the dry run MUST report the composed wave-1 request.

A dry run MUST fail with a typed error on anything that would make the
live request wrong: an unresolved record or location, a render failure,
or an oversize request.
`judge-jev quality` MUST take one or more record ids.

`judge-jev quality` MUST take each record id with one record-kind flag:
`--req` (requirement), `--adr` (architecture decision record) or `--nfr`
(non-functional requirement).
Every record-kind flag of `judge-jev quality` MUST be repeatable.

`judge-jev quality` MUST judge each record with its kind's quality
decision tree (REQ-JEV-0101).

All records of one `judge-jev quality` invocation MUST be logged under
one run name.
`judge-jev validate` MUST take one input file.

`judge-jev validate` MUST take one input-kind flag with that file:
`--tree` (quality tree), `--questions` (question set), `--answers`
(answers file), `--index` (Raptor import index) or `--requests` (batch
request stream).

`judge-jev validate` MUST check the file with the model `judge-jev`
applies to that input kind before its first Jev request (ADR-JEV-0005).
Every refusal from `judge-jev validate` MUST name the field path.

Every refusal from `judge-jev validate` MUST name the rule the field
breaks.

`judge-jev validate --answers` MUST apply the answers-file envelope that
`--answers-file` applies before the first request.
The answers-file envelope MUST require an object of string keys.

The answers-file envelope MUST require each key's value to be an object
or a non-empty list of objects.

The answers-file envelope MUST require an object with `__error__` to hold
only a string code of at most 64 characters.
`judge-jev validate` MUST NOT call Jev.

For every input, every `judge-jev` command MUST print exactly one JSON
object.

The JSON object a `judge-jev` command prints MUST be its result or a
typed error.

`judge-jev` MUST refuse an invalid tree, question set, index, request
stream or run directory before its first Jev request.

`judge-jev` MUST check that every log event of a request (the request,
Jev's largest possible answer and the result) fits the logger's event
size limit before sending the request.

A definition MUST be attachable to a record alone, or to a record and
one location under evaluation.

A request about a record MUST carry, in its state next to the record, only
the definitions attached to that record alone, plus those attached to
that record and the request's location.

A request with no matching definition MUST be identical to the request
sent without definitions.

`judge-jev` MUST refuse, before sending, a request whose definitions take
it over the size limit.

Every request's log event MUST record the digest of each definition it
carried.
`judge-jev` MUST NOT truncate a definition.

`judge-jev` MUST provide a comparison of one or more candidate
definitions.

The comparison MUST run the requests the candidate definitions would
reach with the candidates.
The comparison MUST run the same requests without the candidates.

The comparison MUST report each answer's choice with and without the
candidates.

The comparison MUST report each answer's confidence with and without the
candidates.

The comparison MUST report the candidates as material when an answer's
choice flips or its confidence crosses the decision threshold, and as not
material when every change stays on the same side of the threshold.
The comparison MUST record the threshold it applied.

Every question IRI in one scope (by default the repository) MUST be
declared in one tree file only, across judge-jev's trees and every
consumer extension's.

Every `jj:id` in judge-jev's trees and in every consumer extension's
MUST be unique within its tree.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST validate every tree in the scope against its
schema.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST validate every question set in the scope against
its schema.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST validate every definitions file in the scope
against its schema.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST validate every tree, question set and definitions
file in the scope against the ontology's shapes, including edges and
cycles.
`judge-jev doctor` MUST report each validation failure as an error.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST report a definition with no attachment as a
warning.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST report an attachment to a record the Raptor index
does not hold as a warning.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST report an attachment to a location that does not
exist as a warning.

`judge-jev doctor` MUST report a definition whose source does not exist
as a warning.
`judge-jev doctor` MUST NOT call Jev.
A `judge-jev doctor` warning MUST NOT fail the command.
